title: Jason Quisling chosen to fill retiring Rick Kenin’s VAI board seat
summary: Quisling is senior VP of flight operations and AirCom at Air Methods.
body_markdown:
Jason Quisling. VAI Photo


Jason Quisling, senior VP of flight operations and AirCom at Air Methods, has been selected to fill the VAI board of directors seat vacated by Rick Kenin, 2025–26 VAI chairman and Boston MedFlight COO of transport, who retired Nov. 21, 2026.


Quisling, who is based in Greenwood Village, Colorado, will serve the remainder of Kenin’s term, Nov. 22, 2026, through Jun. 30, 2027, under the large commercial/private operator category.


### **Longtime Aviation Leader**


A dual-rated airline transport pilot and longtime check airman, Quisling has three decades of leadership experience in commercial aviation. He has been with Air Methods, one of the largest air medical emergency services providers in the United States, for 26 years.


“Jason Quisling brings a strong combination of operational leadership, strategic perspective, and regulatory expertise to the VAI board of directors. With 30 years of experience across multiple sectors of vertical aviation and senior leadership responsibility at Air Methods, he offers valuable insight into the needs and challenges of large operators,” said François Lassale, VAI’s president and CEO.


“His experience working with the FAA, NTSB, and federal committees, along with his focus on safety, workforce development, and industry advancement, makes him a valuable contributor to board discussions and VAI’s long-term strategic direction. His broad industry viewpoint and collaborative approach help strengthen VAI’s representation of the operator community.”


As a member of the VAI board, Quisling’s focus will include supporting VAI’s strategic objectives, such as safety, regulatory policy, and workforce development.


“At VAI, I’ll champion data-driven training standards and certification pathways to elevate safety industrywide in a manner that aligns with the association’s strategic objectives,” said Quisling. “I’ll also focus on supporting VAI’s leadership and five-year plan.”


### **A Laudable Legacy**


Kenin leaves VAI with a legacy of strong, commendable leadership during a period of evolution for the association.


“The VAI team extends its sincere thanks to Rick for his leadership and guidance during his time on the VAI board of directors,” Lassale said.


“Rick served during a period of significant change, helping guide the organization through a CEO search and assisting the work of multiple board committees. His commitment, steady leadership, and contributions throughout his tenure have helped set a strong standard for future board service.”


*This press release was prepared and distributed by Vertical Aviation International.*
